extracted.intended_audience: students, dramatists, humorists, and scholars of literary/theatrical comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Principles for creating and evaluating comic character and comic effect in dramatic and literary comedy: what makes a character comic, how comedy differs from tragedy/art, and the observational methods suited to comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gesture vs. Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Gestures ... mean the attitudes, the movements and even the language by which a mental state expresses itself outwardly without any aim or profit ... Gesture, thus defined, is profoundly different from action. Action is intentional or, at any rate, conscious; gesture slips out unawares, it is automatic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy arises when attention is fixed on gesture rather than on action. Action is essential in drama but only accessory in comedy: if we considered only a character's actions (what is meant and willed) we get drama; when we take into account their habitual, automatic gestures (language, attitudes transformed into 'natural gestures') we find them comic. Example: Tartuffe becomes comic when his ingrained hypocritical gestures are noticed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsociability of the performer and spectator insensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsociability in the performer and insensibility in the spectator — such, in a word, are the two essential conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A performer must display a detachment or lack of social responsiveness (unsociability) that makes their behaviour observable as a repeatable fault; the spectator must be kept from full sympathetic/emotional involvement (insensibility) so that laughter, not pathos, is produced. If the spectator's sympathy or aversion is allowed to 'glide along' toward action, the effect becomes dramatic rather than comic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatism / Absentmindedness
rubrics_metrics.description: What is essentially laughable is what is done automatically. In a vice, even in a virtue, the comic is that element by which the person unwittingly betrays himself — the involuntary gesture or the unconscious remark. Absentmindedness is always comical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deeper or more systematic the absentmindedness (e.g., Don Quixote) the stronger the comic effect. Comic sayings that reveal a vice 'in all its nakedness' (where the subject cannot see himself) are especially powerful. Typical devices: contradictions (condemning a conduct and immediately exemplifying it), unconscious remarks, involuntary gestures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigidity / ready-made character
rubrics_metrics.description: If we leave on one side ... that portion which interests our sensibility ... all the rest is capable of becoming comic, and the comic will be proportioned to the rigidity. The ready-made element in our personality, that mechanical element which resembles a piece of clockwork wound up once for all and capable of working automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigidity (fixed, mechanical traits) makes a character imitable and repeatable — hence comic. Such rigidity causes people to 'imitate themselves' and allows others to imitate them; every comic character is a type or stock character. The more the personality crystallises into a fixed type, the more comic it becomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy aims at general types (generality in the work itself)
rubrics_metrics.description: Altogether different is the object of comedy. Here it is in the work itself that the generality lies. Comedy depicts characters we have already come across and shall meet with again. It takes note of similarities. It aims at placing types before our eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike tragedy/art (which aims at individuality and unique inner truth), comedy intentionally constructs general types that can be recognized and reused (titles like Le Misanthrope, L'Avare, Le Distrait). A successful comic work makes its characters exemplars of a class rather than unique individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: External, inductive observation; skin-deep treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy's observation is directed outwards. ... Settling on the surface, it will not be more than skin-deep, dealing with persons at the point at which they come into contact and become capable of resembling one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comic writer observes others from the outside, compares analogous cases, abstracts and generalises (an inductive method) to extract an 'average effect.' Penetrating too far into inner causes or deep individuality will endanger the laughable effect; comedy should localise cause in an intermediate region of the soul so the effect appears average and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use repetition / multiple examples to define types
rubrics_metrics.description: A remarkable instinct ... impels the comic poet, once he has elaborated his central character, to cause other characters, displaying the same general traits, to revolve as satellites round him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish a type, present several different copies/satellites exhibiting the same traits (as the naturalist enumerates varieties to define a species). Collective titles and groups (Les Femmes savantes, Les Précieuses ridicules) highlight types; repetition reinforces the generality and recognizability of the comic trait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy as corrective / social function
rubrics_metrics.description: By reason of their generality and also of their scarcely confessed or scarcely conscious intention to correct and instruct. ... By organising laughter, comedy accepts social life as a natural environment ... it even obeys an impulse of social life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy should select peculiarities that admit reproduction and thus serve to correct or instruct a larger number of people. Its aim is not purely aesthetic disinterestedness but a social corrective: laughter organises social correction by showing faults in a generalisable way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent arousal of strong emotions in the spectator
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether serious or trifling, it is still capable of making us laugh, provided that care be taken not to arouse our emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maintain comic tone, ensure events/characters do not provoke deep sympathy or aversion that would move the audience toward dramatic engagement. If the spectator's emotions are aroused into full sympathy/aversion, the work shifts toward drama or tragedy rather than comedy.
